summary: Redwood AE/SE (Maya + Liam) ran a co-sell pipeline sprint with Verdant Capital to align on a gated pilot for two strategic accounts. Discussion covered partner enablement (playbook, pricing), technical validation paths (hosted vs dedicated, KV cache and batching expectations), security/compliance questions (SSO, KMS, SOC2), procurement timelines, and next steps for benchmarking and exec alignment. Some parts of the transcript have transcription noise; key outcomes are the shared next steps and agreed deadlines.
topics: tech validation: latency/cost targets and benchmark plan
legal: partner addendum and IP/data residency notes
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Aisha (Verdant Head Partnerships), Tom (Verdant Sales Dir), Marta (Verdant Solutions Arch), Neil (Channel Ops), Sophie (Verdant Legal, joined late)
Shared artifacts referenced: Verdant co-sell playbook (drive: /decks/verdant-co-sell-playbook.pdf), benchmark template (sheets: drive.google.com/benchmark-verdant), draft partner addendum (link provided in chat)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, is this a good time?
[00:08] Aisha (Verdant): yes, thanks Maya, sorry bit of background noise on my side, just finishing another standup. 
[00:14] Maya: cool. quick agenda: run through the gated-deal framework, align on pilot accounts and success criteria, scope a short benchmark, and call out any legal/procurement blockers. we'll leave time for q&a.
[00:28] Tom (Verdant): sounds good. from our side we want clarity on revenue split, logo ownership in co-marketing, and how handoffs work if it scales.
[00:35] Liam (Redwood): great, i'll cover the technical validation path — quick note, we use Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput but can run hosted for early pilots to speed things up. also, forgive me if i butcher names in the transcript, the auto transcriber tends to do that.
[00:50] Marta: quick Q up front, when you say 'dedicated' are we talking a managed GPU pool or a physical appliance we host? our infra team cares about network egress and VPC peering.
[01:04] Liam: good point — Redwood Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool in our cloud regions, customer gets isolated capacity and private VPC peering options. for on-prem we do a different package but that wasn't the ask today.
[01:18] Neil: and does that include KMS integration? our security folks require customer-managed keys for some accounts.
[01:25] Maya: yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted we can do envelope encryption and discuss key ownership depending on the contract.
[01:36] Aisha: ok— so high level i think Verdant wants to gate the co-sell: pilot with two logos, if we hit MRR and NPS targets we go wider. need to align on pricing and discounts.
[01:49] Tom: what are typical discount bands for partners? we need to build a plan that supports partner margin and still keeps Redwood unit economics ok.
[01:57] Maya: typically we offer a co-sell referral fee for introductions and a deeper revenue share for joint-sourced deals that reach agreed ARR thresholds. i'll send the pricing grid after this call. for pilots we can do a time-bound promotional rate to accelerate proofs.
[02:14] Marta: can you share a concrete example? like, if pilot spend is $30k, what does Verdant see?
[02:21] Maya: yes — specifics in the doc, but rough example: early pilot promo could be 20% off list, plus a 10% referral fee post-conversion; for joint-sourced and closed deals we tier into 15-25% revenue share depending on commit.
[02:38] Aisha: that helps, thanks.
[02:42] Sophie (Verdant Legal): i'm on now, i skimmed the draft addendum — questions about data residency clauses and audit log retention. some clients require 7 years retention for logs.
[02:55] Liam: audit logs are available in Redwood Console, but retention is configurable as an enterprise add-on. the default hosted retention is 90 days, Dedicated can be extended, and Private gives you full control.
[03:12] Marta: tech question — for the pilot workload we expect avg token lengths of 800-1,200 on generation calls and heavy embedding traffic for search features. what's the expected latency you can hit at that size?
[03:29] Liam: depends on model and quantization. for an open model similar to Mistral 7b or Llama2 13b quantized we typically see p50 generation latencies in the 120-250ms range for short sequences; for 800-1200 tokens you can expect a few seconds end-to-end. our suggestion is batching + KV cache to keep cost down. i'll detail recommendations in the benchmark plan.
[03:52] Tom: are we able to stream partial results? one of our UX folks wants progressive responses.
[03:58] Maya: yes we support streaming and function/tool calling for structured outputs. note: streaming has slightly different SLO behavior under batching.
[04:10] Aisha: ok, gating criteria — what do we want to measure? MRR conversion rate, latency SLO, and product fit (feedback from pilot users)?
[04:20] Maya: agreed. propose: 1) Technical acceptance: average p95 latency < 4s and error rate < 1% over a 2-week run. 2) Business acceptance: 3 pilot accounts commit to a sales cadence and 2 conversion-ready opportunities within 90 days. 3) NPS or product feedback >= X (we'll define).
[04:42] Marta: small nit — p95 <4s is fine but we need p50 targets for user-facing chat. can you add both?
[04:50] Maya: yes, add p50 <1s for short chats; we'll put concrete thresholds in the doc.
[04:57] [05:00] Liam: turning to benchmarks: we propose Redwood runs a two-track test: 1) Hosted pilot with sample traffic to validate functionality and UX; 2) Redwood Dedicated smoke test to prove throughput and cost per token at target scale. we'll provide a benchmarking spreadsheet — we talked about it in the chat (drive.google.com/benchmark-verdant).
[05:20] Neil: for procurement, we need the pilot order form and an estimated SOW. what's the lead time to spin up a Dedicated pool?
[05:28] Maya: typical lead time is 2-3 weeks after contract signature to get Dedicated capacity in place; hosted is immediate.
[05:34] Neil: good to know. that means we can run hosted for the 30-day pilot and then switch. any migration risk?
[05:42] Liam: low — model variants are compatible, KV cache warms differently, but we have automated fallback policies. the main change is routing and infra isolation. we'll document migration steps in the runbook.
[05:58] Tom: pricing question — if we switch from hosted to Dedicated mid-pilot, do we retroactively apply committed pricing?
[06:06] Maya: normally committed pricing is based on the Dedicated contract start date; we can discuss transitional credits if it's a close call — i'll note that as a negotiation item.
[06:16] Marta: security deep dive — we need SAML SSO for our partner portal integration and RBAC for fine-grained access. does Redwood have SSO flows that map to partner roles?
[06:28] Liam: yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported. RBAC exists in the Console; we can tie roles to partner account scopes. for audit we expose detailed event logs. caveat: some older logs use slightly different event names, transcriber might show 'KV cash' in the notes — ignore that.
[06:45] Aisha: haha, noted. Sophie — any immediate legal red flags?
[06:49] Sophie: data residency needs clarity; we have EU customers that require EU-only processing. can Redwood guarantee region pinning for model inference and embeddings?
[06:59] Maya: yes — for Dedicated and Private we can pin to regions and prevent cross-region fallback; hosted sometimes uses multi-region fallbacks unless contractually restricted. we'll add a clause to the addendum.
[07:14] Aisha: thanks, that was one of my big asks.
[07:22] [07:30] Liam: on model variants — we recommend starting with an open LLM variant that balances latency and quality; we can also propose quantized 4-bit variants to lower cost during the pilot. will include model recommendations in the benchmark doc.
[07:45] Tom: what about competitors — we've had prospects ask about Anthropic and LargeCloudAI capabilities; how do we position on performance/cost?
[07:55] Maya: short answer: Redwood is model-agnostic and optimizes serving. we benchmark across similar open models and show per-token cost comparisons; often our advantage is predictable throughput and tooling for rollouts. i'll include a competitive slide.
[08:12] Marta: need to know if you support on-the-fly quantization or it needs a recompile step.
[08:18] Liam: we do quantization-friendly paths in the runtime; some models need a light compile step but it's automated. the user experience is basically a flip in the model config.
[08:30] Aisha: ok — sequencing for us: we want to pick 2 pilot logos next week, sign a pilot SOW week after, then run a 30-60 day pilot. does that timeline sound workable?
[08:43] Maya: yes, workable. i'll send the playbook and a checklist to help you choose the best accounts for a gated pilot.
[08:51] Neil: one operational concern — partner-sourced deals sometimes require co-managed support. what's your support SLA for pilot vs production?
[09:00] Maya: pilots get standard support with an assigned solutions engineer; Dedicated customers can opt into a higher support tier with faster response times and a named CSM. SLA specifics listed in the addendum.
[09:12] Sophie: about IP — some customers want to ensure embeddings are not used to further train public models. we have to make sure there's contractual language about not using customer data for training.
[09:24] Liam: yep, we can put that into the addendum; for Private deployments customers control models and training entirely; for hosted we offer contractual assurances and data-use clauses.
[09:36] [09:45] Aisha: awesome. i want to circle back to the gating criteria — you suggested conversion-ready opportunities in 90 days, is that aggressive?
[09:55] Tom: it depends on the account complexity. some mid-market ones could be faster, enterprise might need longer.
[10:02] Maya: we can make the 90 days a guideline for the pilot plan; for enterprise logos we'll agree extended timelines case-by-case.
[10:10] Marta: one more technical ask — is there a recommended retry policy for transient failures? our engineers want a clear pattern to avoid duplicate side effects.
[10:20] Liam: yes, we recommend idempotency keys for generation calls and exponential backoff on client-side retries. we'll surface a snippet in the runbook.
[10:30] Tom: would be good to have sample code in the partner portal for common languages.
[10:35] Maya: agreed — we'll share SDK snippets and a quickstart repo link in the playbook.
[10:40] [10:45] Aisha: on marketing — if the pilot goes well, Verdant wants joint press and a case study. we need co-branding guidelines.
[10:50] Maya: noted — we have a co-marketing pack; will add it to the playbook.
[10:56] Neil: procurement — i need to map internal purchase order cadence, is there a standard partner invoice flow?
[11:04] Maya: partner billing can be handled via Redwood with partner commission tracked separately; we can also do a pass-through arrangement. i'll have Ops send options.
[11:12] Sophie: legal will do a redline pass once we get the addendum; please include a sample PII handling clause for EU customers.
[11:21] Liam: will do; also include a short checklist for SOC2 evidence and maturity level — that helps speed vendor risk reviews.
[11:29] Aisha: ok, near wrap — any blockers we haven't covered?
[11:33] Marta: none from engineering if we get the benchmark template and expected token distribution.
[11:38] Tom: sales is good, just need the pricing grid.
[11:41] Neil: procurement okay with timelines, will confirm PO cadence.
[11:45] Sophie: legal will review addendum.
[11:48] Maya: recap of next steps: i'll share playbook + pricing grid + co-marketing pack by Thurs (2026-03-05). Liam will run benchmark and share by 2026-03-10. Verdant to pick pilot logos and stakeholders by 2026-03-06. we'll schedule exec alignment week of 3/15.
[12:06] Aisha: thanks all. one last thing — can we get a short exec one-pager that summarizes revenue upside for Verdant and expected timeline?
[12:15] Maya: yes, will add that to the deliverables.
[12:18] [12:22] Liam: quick tech note, i'll include a small matrix comparing expected cost per 1M tokens across model variants and deployment modes.
[12:30] Maya: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
[12:35] Tom: thanks, bye.
[12:36] Aisha: thanks.
[12:37] Marta: bye.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional transcription noise (names and acronyms), timestamps approximate. The audio had a brief dropout around 00:50-01:04 where Aisha's mic cut.
